WSLHD - Trainee - Stage 2 - 4 in Emergency Medicine - Westmead 

Where you'll be working
Westmead Hospital is a key facility of one of Australia's largest major health and medical research precincts and is the principal referral hospital for Western Sydney Local Health District providing district level health services to Parramatta, Holroyd and The Hills Shire LGAs including tertiary and quaternary services to greater Western Sydney, greater metropolitan Sydney, rural NSW and other states. It is a principal referral centre for other metropolitan hospitals within the district including Auburn Hospital, Blacktown and Mount Druitt Hospital.

Westmead Hospital is a leading centre of research, training and specialisation in all fields of Medicine and Dentistry, providing services in Cardiology, Cardiothoracic Surgery, Neurology, Neurosurgery, Kidney and Pancreas transplantation, Cancer Care, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Neonatal Intensive Care, Trauma, Bone Marrow Transplantation, Critical Care, Aged Care and Rehabilitation, Adult Acute Psychiatry (networked with the co-located Cumberland Hospital) as well as other specialised medical and surgical services.

The Westmead Hospital Emergency Department (ED) operates 24 hours, 7 days per week and manages all types and levels of illnesses and injuries. As one of six major trauma centres in the state, the ED also cares for people with the most severe physical injuries. Westmead Hospital ED presentation numbers are among the highest in the state, currently around 80,000 per year.

Westmead Hospital is one of Australia's largest centres for postgraduate training to specialist levels in all fields with over 100 PhD students and other postgraduate students supervised by Westmead Hospital scientists and clinicians. Westmead is home to internationally recognised institutes of health research, the most prominent being the Westmead Millennium Institute. The Westmead Millennium Institute is one of the largest medical research institutes in Australia, conducting research into a wide range of human disorders affecting both adults and children, including infectious and immune diseases, cancer and leukaemia, liver and metabolic diseases, eye and brain related disorders and heart and respiratory disorders.

Cumberland Hospital, co- located with Westmead Hospital provides primary and secondary mental health services to the local population and tertiary acute, extended and forensic mental health services to greater western Sydney and NSW. There is also a range of community mental health residential facilities, recovery support and specialist treatment services located on the campus.

What you'll be doing
WSLHD - Trainee - Stage 2 - 4 in Emergency Medicine - Westmead 
The primary purpose of the Trainee Stage 2-4 in the Emergency Department is to provide clinical care, under appropriate supervision, to patients requiring emergency medical services in a complex clinical environment. This position will provide experience in a critical care environment and have responsibilities and opportunities for autonomous practice commensurate with the level of experience of the incumbent.
The Trainee Stage 2-4 is expected to supervise and also participate in teaching Junior Medical Officers and Medical Students, and taking part in research where appropriate.

 

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

MBBS or equivalent, currently registered or eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia

Must have completed at least four postgraduate years training including a minimum 12 months full time Emergency Medicine experience in an Australian Public Hospital or equivalent (not as an Observer)

Demonstrated ability to work independently in a supervised environment with commitment to self-education and continuous professional development.

Ability to work effectively as part of a multi-disciplinary team with an understanding of the roles of the doctor and other members of the healthcare team

Ability and willingness to work at the facilities within the Network to deliver patient care. Ability and willingness to participate in a rotating roster including days, evenings, nights and weekends and preparedness to participate in an on call roster for the emergency department.

Excellent organisational and time management skills and ability to manage competing priorities in a complex environment.

Demonstrated commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your Role at St John of God Midland Public Hospital 

St John of God Midland Public Hospital provides high-quality public and private services to people living in the east metropolitan and Wheatbelt regions. Midland is one of our busiest hospitals, with demand for public services consistently increasing every year, making it a dynamic and fast-paced environment to work in.

St John of God Midland Hospital is seeking a motivated and highly capable Colorectal Fellow - Senior Registrar to join our established and progressive colorectal unit for a comprehensive full-time 12-month fellowship, starting February 2027.

Supervised by four experienced colorectal surgeons, the Fellowship is designed to develop expertise in the assessment, management and surgical treatment of the full spectrum of colorectal disease. The Fellow will gain extensive hands-on experience in advanced laparoscopic and minimally invasive colorectal surgery, while developing skills in perioperative decision-making, multidisciplinary care coordination, leadership and clinical research.

The SJOG Midland Colorectal Unit is a high-volume service performing more than 150 colectomies annually and is recognised for its collaborative approach to patient care, working closely with Gastroenterology, Gynaecology, Oncology and Psycho-Oncology services. The faculty maintains strong national and international professional links, is actively involved in research and education, and includes surgeons who currently hold or have held leadership positions within CSSANZ, RACS and the WA Colorectal Cancer Collaborative.

Fellowship Highlights

Dedicated colorectal outpatient clinics.

Exposure to more than 100 elective and emergency public colectomies annually.

Elective benign and malignant colorectal surgery, including inflammatory bowel disease.

Participation in colorectal and emergency on-call services.

Proctology and anal manometry experience.

Access to both colonoscopy and upper GI endoscopy lists with colorectal surgeons and gastroenterologists.

Exposure to advanced laparoscopic, minimally invasive and robotic surgical techniques.

Private assisting opportunities, including complex colorectal and gynae-colorectal cases.

Supervision and mentoring opportunities with SET and non-accredited surgical trainees.

Research, Leadership and Innovation

The Fellow will have access to the unit's unique Colorectal Cancer Database (CIC), incorporating PROMs, and GSTAR, the colorectal morbidity and outcomes database, providing excellent opportunities for research, quality improvement, presentations and publication. Dedicated colorectal nursing, data management and project support enable meaningful academic output throughout the Fellowship.

The role also provides valuable leadership experience through teaching and supervising junior medical staff, participating in audit and morbidity review processes, and contributing to clinical governance and service improvement initiatives.

The unit continues to lead innovation in Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) and is actively developing overnight colectomy pathways, providing exposure to contemporary models of perioperative colorectal care.

The 2027 Fellowship is part-funded through a Medtronic educational grant and is seeking CSSANZ accreditation for the 2028 training year.

This Fellowship offers an outstanding opportunity for advanced colorectal training within a high-volume, academically active and progressive colorectal service.

To be successful in this role

You will Hold current registration as a Medical Practitioner with the Medical Board of Australia (AHPRA) and be an advanced Royal Australasian College of Surgeons (RACS) SET trainee, Fellow, or possess equivalent surgical training and experience.

You will be able to demonstrate strong clinical and procedural skills within colorectal surgery, general surgery, or a comparable surgical environment and have a genuine interest in pursuing advanced training and a career in colorectal surgery.

Above all, you place patients at the centre of your practice and are committed to supporting our Mission and Values in every aspect of your work.

We can offer you:

Salary: $188,817 - $198,142 per annum, plus 12% superannuation

Professional development allowance $16,747 pro rata per Annum if part time

A welcoming and supportive culture

Salary packaging up to $18,550 on a range of benefits such as mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, holiday accommodation or other everyday living expenses as well as options to salary package benefits above the FBT cap on items such as:

Novated leasing 

work related expenses

self-education and

additional superannuation

A healthy work-life balance through flexible work options, additional purchased leave and well-being programs

Employee discount on St John of God Hospital & Medical Services and Private Health Insurance

Employee support through our dedicated free Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Opportunities for education and professional development

* All applicants are asked to submit a covering letter (of no more than two (2) pages) demonstrating how you meet the requirements of the role

For enquiries about this position, applicants should contact Mary Theophilus, ph. 9462 4488

Agency applications will not be considered

The Westmead Hospital Emergency Department (ED) operates 24 hours, 7 days per week and manages all types and levels of illnesses and injuries. As one of six major trauma centres in the state, the ED also cares for people with the most severe physical injuries.

Westmead Hospital ED presentation numbers are among the highest in the state Critical care services within Westmead Hospital are provided by the Intensive care unit and the medical and surgical high dependency units. What you'll be doing
WSLHD - Provisional Fellow - Trauma Surgery 
The Provisional Fellow will be responsible for overseeing the care of trauma patients admitted to the Trauma Unit. He- She will be expected to function at the level of a junior consultant. Clinical trauma nursing staff support includes Trauma Clinical Nurse Consultants and Trauma Registered Nurses. The Provisional Fellow will be expected to provide leadership at all Major Trauma calls during business hours, and when on-call. He- She is also expected to be available to assist in major trauma cases if required at other times. He-she is expected to supervise and teach the junior members of the Trauma Unit. The Provisional Fellow will be supervised by the Trauma Consultant of the week. These positions are accredited by the Australia New Zealand Association for the Surgery of Trauma for post-fellowship training in trauma.
